To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the S100 protein family regulates the TPR protein family through a novel Ca2+-signalling pathway.
the S100A2/S100A6-TPR protein interactions regulate the Hsp70-Hsp90-Hop complex and KLC-cargoligand interaction in a Ca2 +-regulated manner.
S100A proteins interact with several target TPR proteins and regulate their ligand-binding properties in vivo and in vitro.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and characterization of novel targets of the Ca2+-regulated S100 proteins.
understanding the role of the S100A2, S100A6 and other S100 proteins in intracellular signaling pathways and in the development and progression of cancer.
the interactions of S100A6 and S100A2 with the TPR motif containing proteins Hop and KLC.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the S100A2- and S100A2-associated proteins (e.g. HOP, KLC, Tom70) are novel targets for S100 proteins.
the S100A2/S100A6 proteins are novel regulators of Hsp70/Hop/Hsp90 and KLC/ cargo complex formation via Ca2+-regulated interactions with the TPR domains of Hop and KLC.
the S100A2-TPR and S100A2-KLC interactions are regulated by Ca2+, which results in inhibition of Hop-Hsp70, Hop-Hsp90, KLC-JIP-1, and Tom70-ligands interactions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
S100 proteins interact with TPR proteins and modulate their functions via Ca2+-signalling.
the S100A2/A6-TPR motif complex formation is an important step to regulate the chaperone complex formation or the kinesin-cargo interaction in a Ca2+ -dependent manner.
the S100 protein-TRP protein complex formation regulates chaperone complex formation, JNK signaling, and protein import.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the TPR domain is a novel Ca2+-binding domain.

S100 proteins regulate protein-protein interactions through Ca2+-dependent interactions with the TPR motif-containing proteins, Hsp90-Hsp70-organiz-ing protein, kinesin light chains, and Tom70, and that this regulation may play an important role in intracellular Ca2+ signaling pathways.
S100A protein family can regulate the activity of TPR proteins by direct binding.
